sentences._hearing_file: Ram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: Shri Yash Soni - Dy. Advocate General for State.
sentences._hearing_file: Ram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: Heard on I.A.No.31454/2024, which is second application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant No.2-Mangal.
sentences._hearing_file: Ram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: His first application was dismissed on merits vide order dated 13.02.2023.
sentences._hearing_file: Ram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: The appellant No.2 has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 376(D) of IPC and sentenced to undergo for Life Imprisonment with fine of Rs.2,000/- and Section 366 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.1,000/- respectively, with default stipulations.
sentences._hearing_file: Ram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant No.2 submits that he is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the matter.
sentences._hearing_file: Ram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: He also submits that the other co- accused namely, Ram has already been granted bail by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 14.11.2024.
sentences._hearing_file: Ram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is contended that as per prosecution version the prosecutrix was married and major lady on the date of incident in the year 2019.
sentences._hearing_file: Ram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is contended that as per prosecution version the prosecutrix had voluntarily left her matrimonial home as well as her 2 CRA-12327-2022 parents home and started to live in the accommodation provided by co- accused Chhote Pawar and during that period it is alleged that the present appellant along with other co-accused persons committed the offence of sexual assault in terms of Section 376 and other corresponding offences against the prosecutrix.
sentences._hearing_file: Ram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is further contended that as per medical report there are no injury found on the internal organs and private part of the prosecutrix.
sentences._hearing_file: Ram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is further contended that as per the DNA report DNA has been matched with co-accused Chhote Pawar and DNA did not match with present appellant and though the DNA report found presence of male DNA but that male DNA matched with co-accused Chhote on the under garments of the prosecutrix.
sentences._hearing_file: Ram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is contended that the appellant No.2 has already spent more than 5 years in actual custody and there is no likelihood of the appeal being heard in near future because the appeal is of the year 2022.
sentences._hearing_file: Ram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: Per contra learned counsel for the State has objected to grant of suspension of remaining jail sentence of the appellant on the basis of the averments made in the written objection.
sentences._hearing_file: Ram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Considering the aforesaid but without expressing any conclusive opinion on merits of the case and coupled with the fact that final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future, we deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant no.2.

sentences._hearing_file: Ram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant No.2-Mangal hereby suspended and 3 CRA-12327-2022 it is directed that appellant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 17.11.2025 and also on such other dates, as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.

opennyai_summary.facts:
His first application was dismissed on merits vide order dated 13.02.2023.
The appellant No.2 has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 376(D) of IPC and sentenced to undergo for Life Imprisonment with fine of Rs.2,000/- and Section 366 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.1,000/- respectively, with default stipulations.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is contended that as per prosecution version the prosecutrix had voluntarily left her matrimonial home as well as her 2 CRA-12327-2022 parents home and started to live in the accommodation provided by co- accused Chhote Pawar and during that period it is alleged that the present appellant along with other co-accused persons committed the offence of sexual assault in terms of Section 376 and other corresponding offences against the prosecutrix.
It is further contended that as per the DNA report DNA has been matched with co-accused Chhote Pawar and DNA did not match with present appellant and though the DNA report found presence of male DNA but that male DNA matched with co-accused Chhote on the under garments of the prosecutrix.
Per contra learned counsel for the State has objected to grant of suspension of remaining jail sentence of the appellant on the basis of the averments made in the written objection.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
Considering the aforesaid but without expressing any conclusive opinion on merits of the case and coupled with the fact that final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future, we deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant no.2.

List the matter for final hearing in due course.
